subject.title: fix(secrets): add audit check severity threshold

question: Should OpenClaw accept a public `openclaw secrets audit --severity-min` threshold for check-mode gates on secrets audit findings?
rationale: The implementation is clean and default-compatible, but deciding whether info-level audit findings may be non-blocking for operator automation is a security/product policy choice on a CODEOWNERS-protected secrets surface.

options.title: Close Until Sponsored
options.body: Close this contributor PR for now and invite a secops/core CLI owner to reopen or sponsor the threshold if the audit policy is accepted.

options.title: Sponsor Current Flag
options.body: Accept the opt-in public CLI contract because plain `--check` still fails on any finding and the PR includes docs, tests, CI, and terminal proof.

options.title: Request Narrower Policy
options.body: Ask for a narrower owner-approved gate, such as limiting the threshold by finding class or moving the policy into a broader audit/doctor design.

recommendation.title: Close Until Sponsored
recommendation.body: Close this contributor PR for now and invite a secops/core CLI owner to reopen or sponsor the threshold if the audit policy is accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: Josh has the strongest feature-history connection to the secrets audit flow and its CLI/docs contract, while secops review can cover the security policy angle.
